newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says running final tests on Maghreb pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says running final tests on Maghreb pipeline.

text.p: The Maghreb gas pipeline linking Algeria's main Hassi R'mel field to European markets in Spain and Portugal is undergoing final tests in the section crossing Morocco, an Algerian energy official said on Tuesday.

"Increase-in-pressure tests started on (Tuesday) September 3 until September 9 in the section of the pipeline through Morocco and the same work will be carried out on September 10 in the Gibraltar section," he told Reuters by telephone from Algiers.
Some 530 km (330 miles) of the 1,375 km (860 mile) pipeline -- built at a cost of some $2.2 billion -- runs through Morocco.
The official said the section under the Strait of Gibraltar to Cordoba in Spain, had been tested by gas being pumped in on July 25.

Manuel Fontanilla Torres, project manager in Morocco for the Maghreb-Europe Pipeline, told an International Energy Agency gas conference in Berlin on Tuesday that the pipeline was now being filled with gas before the start of operations next month.
The line threads through southern Algeria to Morocco, with 45 km (28 miles) offshore before it reaches Spain and then on to Portugal.
The 48-inch pipeline will have a capacity of 9.5 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year when it is officially inaugurated early in November.
This capacity may be expanded in a second phase to 18.5 bcm a year to supply thirsty European markets in France and Germany.

Algerian energy officials on Tuesday quoted the North African country's Energy and Mining Minister Amar Makhloufi as saying this week the pipeline will be officially opened on November 1. This will coincide with celebrations for Algeria's independence war against French colonial rule.
Officials said the pipeline will be ready for the start up of commercial operations on October 25.
"But the (Algerian) energy minister had said the pipeline will be inaugurated in November 1. There is no big difference between the two dates. It will be only a week," one said.
Fontanilla Torres said the "line construction is finished. Now we have tested it, we are putting gas into the line and expect to finish this by the end of the month."
"We will then bring it up to pressure of 50 bars and we will commence operation in October".
